info.title: openmediavault-webui contract
info.description: The backend methods the openmediavault web interface calls, described from OMV's source and from replies captured on a test system. Nothing on the server reads this document.

post.description: Sign in with a user name and password. Wrong credentials are HTTP 400; too many failed second-factor attempts for the user are HTTP 429. Never retried automatically (UI-14).

429.description: Too many failed second-factor attempts for this user. The reply says no wait time (A10).

post.description: Answer the pending challenge of Session.login. HTTP 400 for a wrong code; 429 from the third failure on, with a growing delay; 401 when no login is pending or it expired (A10).

401.description: No login is pending, or it expired (300 s) or was discarded by another call.

429.description: Too many wrong codes. The delay grows from 5 s to 300 s; the reply does not say how long (A10).

post.description: End the session. Returns null.
Host, version, load and memory, and whether configuration changes are pending. A user gets only the time and host name.

401.description: No session, or it ended. The first call after the idle timeout says so; later ones say there is no session (A3).

post.description: True when saved settings have not been applied yet.
Deploy the pending configuration changes, as a background task. Services may restart. The task's result is the list of modules deployed.
Throw away every saved change that has not been applied, as a background task. Nothing is deployed.
Used only by the task helper. Not read-only: the last poll of a finished task deletes it on the server (A6).

500.description: The task failed: the message is the task's whole output (for an apply, the Salt log). Also the answer for a handle the server has already deleted (A6).

post.description: Used only by the task helper, and not for polling: on a finished task it deletes the task, so a later getOutput fails.
Used only by the task helper. Ends the task; the handle is gone afterwards. Returns null.
The SSH service settings.
Save the SSH settings. Nothing changes on the system until the pending changes are applied. Returns the stored settings.
A page of shared folders, sorted and searched by the backend.

post.summary: File systems that can hold a shared folder
post.description: OMV's own list of the file systems a new shared folder may be made on: each mount entry that is mounted now, is not a bind mount, and whose file system type can hold a shared folder, with the mount entry's UUID that ShareMgmt.set takes. It checks each mount folder but reads no file. Changes nothing.

post.summary: Make or change a shared folder
post.description: Store a shared folder. With OMV's placeholder UUID it makes a new one: the record is written first, then its folder is made on the disk at once if it does not exist (on BTRFS, as a subvolume), with the file mode sent, the group every person belongs to and the setgid mark; a folder that exists is used as it is, with its files and file permissions. On an existing shared folder it rewrites the record and keeps the access list. OMV refuses a name already taken (exact case) and a path already used on the same file system. It does not check that the file system is mounted; the interface makes folders only on file systems ShareMgmt.getCandidates and its own reading offer. Marks the sharedfolders and systemd modules dirty, and on a change also the modules of what uses the folder, such as samba. Returns the stored folder.

500.description: OMV refused: a shared folder with that name, or with that path on the same file system, already exists.

post.summary: Set who can use a shared folder
post.description: Replace a shared folder's whole access list: an entry left out is removed. Access decides who the SMB and Rsync servers let in; it changes no file permission on the disk. OMV refuses an account that does not exist and the web interface's administrator account, and then nothing changes. Nothing reaches the network until the pending changes are applied; it marks the sharedfolders and systemd modules dirty, and samba when the folder has an SMB share. It can take access away, so it is a service-level change.

500.description: OMV refused an entry: the account does not exist, or it is the web interface's administrator account.

post.summary: Delete a shared folder, keeping its files or with them
post.description: Delete a shared folder. OMV refuses while any setting refers to it: an SMB share (even one turned off), an NFS share, an Rsync server module, a backup job, the home folders setting or an add-on. With `recursive` false it removes only the shared folder's record and every file stays on the disk. With `recursive` true it first refuses when another shared folder uses the same folder or one inside it, then deletes the folder on the disk and everything in it, inside the request (not a background task; the deletion cannot be undone), then removes the record. Both mark the sharedfolders and systemd modules dirty. Returns the deleted folder.

500.description: OMV refused: a setting refers to the folder, or (with its files) another shared folder uses the same folder or one inside it.

post.summary: People who can be given access
post.description: A page of the accounts that are not system accounts, sorted and searched by the backend, each with what OMV stores about it. The interface reads the whole list and shows only each name and description. Changes nothing.

post.summary: Groups that can be given access
post.description: A page of the groups that are not system groups, sorted and searched by the backend. Changes nothing.
The SMB/CIFS service's settings, without its shares: whether it is on, and the workgroup, home-folder and protocol options the classic interface sets. Changes nothing.

post.summary: Turn Windows and Mac sharing on or off
post.description: Store the SMB/CIFS service's settings. The interface sends the whole SMB.getSettings reply with only `enable` changed. With `enable` true OMV refuses a NAS name longer than 15 characters. Turning it off makes every shared folder unreachable from Windows and Mac computers once applied; nothing is lost. Nothing changes on the system until the pending changes are applied; it marks the samba and avahi modules dirty. Returns the stored settings.

500.description: OMV refused to turn it on, such as for a NAS name longer than 15 characters.

post.summary: Shared folders shared with Windows and Mac computers
post.description: The SMB shares, each as stored with the name of its shared folder. The interface reads the whole list. Changes nothing.

500.description: The read failed because a share names a shared folder whose record is gone (removed by hand, outside OMV's own checks); the message is OMV's internal one.

post.summary: Share a folder with Windows and Mac computers, or change how
post.description: Store an SMB share. With OMV's placeholder UUID it makes one; otherwise it replaces the stored one with what is sent, so a field left out returns to its default. OMV refuses a second share for the same shared folder and does not check that the shared folder exists. Time Machine turns macOS compatibility on. Nothing reaches the network until the pending changes are applied; it marks the samba and avahi modules dirty. Returns the stored share.

500.description: OMV refused, such as a second share for the same shared folder.

post.summary: Stop sharing a folder with Windows and Mac computers
post.description: Remove an SMB share's record, with every option set on it. It touches no shared folder, no access list and no file. Computers using the share lose it once the pending changes are applied; it marks the samba and avahi modules dirty. Returns the removed share.
The signed-in user's own account.
How long the server keeps an idle session before ending it. Every signed-in user can read it.
The web interface's ports, whether it is served over HTTPS, and the session timeout.

Stop showing the first-sign-in welcome to every administrator, in every browser (`displayWelcomeMessage` in System.getInformation becomes false). Takes effect at once; nothing is left pending. Calling it again when the welcome is already dismissed also succeeds. No method shows the welcome again. Returns null.

Save the signed-in user's own e-mail address and description. The server refuses it (HTTP 500) for a system account such as `admin`, and for an account the administrator does not let its user change (`_readonly` in UserMgmt.getUserByContext). The account changes at once; the mail settings (and the SSH settings, when the account has SSH keys) are left pending. Returns the stored account.

200.description: The method's response value, without the fields in x-omv-omit.

500.description: The account may not be changed by its user.

post.description: Change the signed-in user's own password. It takes effect at once. The backend does not check `_readonly` here; the interface does. For an account OMV manages (not a system account such as `admin`), the server also leaves the mail settings, and the SSH settings when the account has SSH keys, pending (observed on OMV 8.6.1). Returns null.
The system's host name and domain name.
The time zone, whether the clock is set from time servers, and the server's current date.

How the system sends notification e-mail. The server's reply also carries the SMTP password in plain text; the transport removes it before the reply is validated, cached or returned (UI-6), so no page can show or keep it.

200.description: The method's response value, without the fields in x-omv-omit.

post.description: Every configured file system that is mounted now, with its size and usage. The server measures each one as it answers, so a file system on a sleeping disk can make the reply slow. It does not read S.M.A.R.T.

Every file system configured in OMV, with whether it is available, being created or missing, paged and sorted by the backend. Unlike enumerateMountedFilesystems, it lists a configured file system whose disk is gone (status 3). The server looks for every file system on every disk and measures the mounted ones as it answers, so it is heavier than that method; `limit` null lists every row.

Every file system the system detects, whether or not OMV has set it up, as a plain list: the system's own root and boot file systems, swap space (type "swap") and file systems from another computer included, which FileSystemMgmt.getList leaves out. FileSystemMgmt.getList calls this method itself and adds OMV's mount entries to its result, so reading it touches the disks no more than getList does. The server measures each mounted file system as it answers. Changes nothing.

Read the S.M.A.R.T. health of every disk that supports it, as a background task. The task's result is the list of disks. It changes no setting, but it runs smartctl on every disk without sparing sleeping ones, so it can wake them: the interface starts it only when the user asks for it. The parameters are checked inside the task, so a wrong one makes the task fail.
Whether each service is turned on and whether it is running. The server asks systemd about each service as it answers.

Who is connected to the SMB/CIFS shares and which files they have open (smbstatus). The reply is the commands' text as they print it. It fails while the service's settings have changes not yet applied, because the text would describe the old settings.

500.description: The samba module has configuration changes that are not applied yet (ConfigDirtyException): "Please apply the configuration changes first."

post.description: The NFS shares exported now and their options (exportfs). The reply is the commands' text as they print it. It fails while the service's settings have changes not yet applied, because the text would describe the old settings.

500.description: The nfs module has configuration changes that are not applied yet (ConfigDirtyException): "Please apply the configuration changes first."

post.description: Who is signed in and which SSH connections are open (who and lsof). The reply is the commands' text as they print it. It fails while the service's settings have changes not yet applied, because the text would describe the old settings.

500.description: The ssh module has configuration changes that are not applied yet (ConfigDirtyException): "Please apply the configuration changes first."

post.description: A page of the system's network interfaces, sorted by the backend, including the loopback interface "lo". The backend ignores `search`. A configured Wi-Fi interface's reply carries a secret, never shown (UI-6).

200.description: The method's response value, without the fields in x-omv-omit.

post.description: A page of one system log, parsed into rows, sorted and searched by the backend. Every call re-reads and parses the whole log (its last 100000 lines at most), whatever page is asked for: read a log once and page it in the browser. Log lines can name users, hosts and addresses; they are shown as text.

500.description: The log id is not one the server knows.

post.description: The system's load, memory and processes, as top reports them at one moment. The server runs top for about a second for each call.

Every disk the system can see, including read-only ones such as an optical drive, as a plain list in no particular order. It asks smartctl not to wake a disk that is in standby (--nocheck=standby), so it spares sleeping disks: such a disk reports its power mode as STANDBY and no temperature. Changes nothing.

The disks of enumerateDevices, each with its stored power and cache settings (`hdparm`) when it has any, paged and sorted by the backend; `limit` null lists every disk. It answers at once (the stock interface calls it as a background task, getListBg, which this contract does not use). It asks smartctl not to wake a disk that is in standby (--nocheck=standby), so it spares sleeping disks: such a disk reports its power mode as STANDBY and no temperature. Changes nothing.
One stored power and cache settings object, by its UUID (the `hdparm.uuid` of DiskMgmt.getList). Fails when there is no such object. Read from the configuration; it does not touch the disk.

Create a disk's power and cache settings (with OMV's placeholder UUID) or change them. The disk must exist; the server stores its /dev/disk/by-id/ link and refuses a second settings object for the same disk. Nothing changes on the system until the pending changes are applied; it marks the smartmontools module dirty. Applying it sets these values on every disk that has settings. Returns the stored settings.

Erase a disk, as a background task. A quick wipe (`secure` false) removes the partition table and the file system, RAID and other signatures at both ends of the disk, in seconds; a secure wipe overwrites the whole disk once and can take hours. Everything on the disk is lost and cannot be recovered. Before calling it the interface itself refuses the system disk, a read-only disk and a disk that holds a mounted file system or a RAID member (journal, 2026-11-21). The task's output is the commands' log text; it has no result. Changes no configuration, so nothing is pending afterwards.

Ask the disk controllers to look for disks added or resized since the system started. Returns null at once; a new disk can take a few seconds to appear in the lists. Changes no configuration and wakes no disk.

Every physical disk OMV can read S.M.A.R.T. data from, with its health, as a plain list in no particular order. OMV counts every ATA, SCSI and NVMe disk, so a disk whose smartctl reports no S.M.A.R.T. support is listed as BAD_STATUS (observed for the test VM's virtual SATA disks). It runs smartctl on every disk without sparing sleeping ones, so it can wake them: the interface reads it only when the user asks. One smartctl runs per disk, so it is slow with many disks. Changes nothing.

The disks of Smart.enumerateDevices whose S.M.A.R.T. monitoring is turned on: the disks the stock interface offers for a scheduled self-test. It reads every disk as enumerateDevices does, so it can wake sleeping disks: the interface reads it only when the user asks. Changes nothing.
The S.M.A.R.T. monitoring settings for every disk. Read from the configuration only; it does not touch the disks.

Save the S.M.A.R.T. monitoring settings for every disk. Nothing changes on the system until the pending changes are applied; it marks the smartmontools module dirty. When applied, the monitoring service starts or stops as `enable` says. Returns the stored settings; the reply also carries `monitor` and `scheduledtests` as empty strings (observed on OMV 8.6.1), which are not settings and are not described here.

One disk's stored S.M.A.R.T. monitoring settings, found by any of the disk's device files, with whether a scheduled self-test refers to the disk. A disk has none until they are first saved, and then this fails with HTTP 500: Smart.getListBg gives such a disk OMV's placeholder UUID, so the interface asks only for a disk whose `uuid` is not the placeholder. Read from the configuration and the system's device list; it does not run smartctl and wakes no disk.

500.description: The disk has no stored monitoring settings. The message names the configuration query.

post.description: Create one disk's S.M.A.R.T. monitoring settings (with OMV's placeholder UUID) or change them. The disk must exist and be one OMV reads S.M.A.R.T. data from; the server stores its /dev/disk/by-id/ link and the smartctl device type, and refuses a second settings object for the same disk. The stock interface does not let monitoring be turned off while a scheduled self-test refers to the disk (`_used` of getDeviceSettings). Nothing changes on the system until the pending changes are applied; it marks the smartmontools module dirty. Returns the stored settings.

What smartctl reports about one disk: model, serial number, firmware, capacity, health and the rest of its information section, as display text keyed by name, with the temperature, power cycles and power-on hours where OMV finds them. It runs smartctl on the disk without sparing it when asleep, so it can wake a sleeping disk: the interface reads it only when the user asks. Changes nothing.

The S.M.A.R.T. attributes of an ATA disk, each with OMV's assessment. NVMe and SAS disks report their health in another form and answer an empty list (observed for the test VM's NVMe disk), as does a disk without S.M.A.R.T. It runs smartctl on the disk without sparing it when asleep, so it can wake a sleeping disk: the interface reads it only when the user asks. Changes nothing.

The short and extended self-tests an ATA disk has run, newest first, with how each ended. NVMe disks answer an empty list (observed on the test VM). It runs smartctl on the disk without sparing it when asleep, so it can wake a sleeping disk: the interface reads it only when the user asks. Changes nothing.

The full smartctl report for one disk (its --xall output) as one block of text. It runs smartctl on the disk without sparing it when asleep, so it can wake a sleeping disk: the interface reads it only when the user asks. Changes nothing.

Every scheduled S.M.A.R.T. self-test, each with its disk as the system sees it now, paged and sorted by the backend; `limit` null lists every test. A test whose disk is not present is still listed, with an empty device file. Read from the configuration and the system's device list; it does not run smartctl and wakes no disk.
One scheduled S.M.A.R.T. self-test, by its UUID, as stored (its disk by the /dev/disk/by-id/ link). Fails when there is no such test. Read from the configuration only.

Create a scheduled S.M.A.R.T. self-test (with OMV's placeholder UUID) or change one. The disk must exist and be one OMV reads S.M.A.R.T. data from; the stock interface offers only monitored disks (enumerateMonitoredDevices). The server stores the disk's /dev/disk/by-id/ link. Nothing changes on the system until the pending changes are applied; it marks the smartmontools module dirty. The test runs on its schedule once applied. Returns the stored test.

Delete one scheduled S.M.A.R.T. self-test, by its UUID. Only the schedule is removed; the disk and its self-test log are not touched, and discarding the pending changes brings the test back. Nothing changes on the system until the pending changes are applied; it marks the smartmontools module dirty. Returns the deleted test.

Start a scheduled test's self-test on its disk now, as a background task. The task ends once smartctl has started the test; the disk then runs it by itself (a short test for minutes, a long one for hours) and records the outcome in its self-test log. It wakes the disk and slows it while the test runs. The task's output is smartctl's text; it has no result. Fails at once with HTTP 500 when the test's disk has no stored monitoring settings. Changes no configuration.

500.description: The test's disk has no stored monitoring settings, or there is no such test.

post.description: Every software RAID array with its member devices, from the RAID plugin (openmediavault-md). The server asks mdadm and the kernel's RAID status, and the configuration for whether an array is in use; it does not run smartctl. Changes nothing. A member's role (working, spare, rebuilding, failed) is not here: `devices` lists failed members and spares alike, and MdMgmt.getDetail says which is which. When the plugin is not installed, OMV does not know the service and the call fails with HTTP 404, code 0 and the message "RPC service 'MdMgmt' not found." (observed on OMV 8.6.1): the transport throws an RpcError with `status` 404, the only reply of this method with that status. Read that as "no RAID plugin, so no RAID members"; any other failure means the arrays could not be read.

404.description: The RAID plugin is not installed: OMV knows no MdMgmt service. Code 0, message "RPC service 'MdMgmt' not found.".

post.description: mdadm's report on one array, as display text: its facts, then one line per member with what that member is doing (working, spare, rebuilding, failed, missing). It is the only reply that says what each member is doing. The server asks mdadm, which reads the kernel's state; it does not run smartctl. Changes nothing. An array that does not exist fails with HTTP 500.

500.description: There is no such array.

post.description: The disks an array lists as its members, with their sizes and serial numbers, from the system's device information. A member that is no longer present is left out. It says nothing of what each member is doing: MdMgmt.getDetail does. Changes nothing. An array that does not exist fails with HTTP 500.

post.summary: Disks that can go into an array
post.description: The disks the RAID plugin offers for a new array or for adding to one: not read-only, not connected by USB, not named by another service's settings, not in use, and with nothing found on them (no partition table, file system, or RAID or other signature). A disk taken out of an array keeps the array's marks and is not offered until it is erased. The server asks the system's device information and the configuration; it reads no array member's superblock (unlike enumerateDevices, getDetail and getSlaves), so the interface uses it to learn whether the plugin is installed (journal, 2026-11-21). Changes nothing. When the plugin is not installed, OMV does not know the service and the call fails with HTTP 404 "RPC service 'MdMgmt' not found.".

404.description: The RAID plugin is not installed: OMV knows no MdMgmt service. Code 0, message "RPC service 'MdMgmt' not found.".

post.description: Erase the disks given and make them into a new array at the next free /dev/mdN, at once. Every disk is overwritten and what was on it is lost; the server checks nothing about the disks first, not that they are candidates, empty or not the system disk, so the interface itself refuses every disk its candidate list and the disk-use model do not both allow (journal, 2026-11-21). A "stripe" (RAID0) has no protection: if one disk fails, everything on all of them is lost. The request returns as soon as mdadm has made the array; a mirror, RAID5, RAID6 or RAID10 then synchronises its disks in the kernel for minutes or hours (MdMgmt.enumerateDevices shows it), and can be used meanwhile. Marks the mdadm and initramfs modules dirty (observed on the test VM): applying them writes the arrays down so the NAS starts them under the same names, and rebuilds the start-up image. Returns the plugin's change record.

post.summary: Add a disk to an array
post.description: Erase a disk and add it to an array, at once. Added to an array that is short of a disk, it replaces the missing one and the kernel rebuilds onto it for minutes or hours; added to an array that has all its disks, it becomes a spare, which takes over by itself when a disk fails. The array does not get bigger (MdMgmt.grow does that). What was on the disk is lost, and the server checks nothing about it, not even that it is as large as the array's disks: the interface itself refuses every disk its candidate list and the disk-use model do not both allow. Marks the mdadm and initramfs modules dirty (observed on the test VM). Returns the plugin's change record.

post.summary: Make an array bigger with more disks
post.description: Erase the disks given, add them to an array, and make the array use them: the server adds them first (as spares), then tells mdadm to use every disk. This cannot be undone: an array is never made smaller again. The request returns at once; the kernel then reshapes the array for hours, often a day or more on large disks, and the NAS must not be turned off meanwhile (MdMgmt.enumerateDevices shows it). The array's size grows when the reshape ends; the file system on it is grown afterwards on its own (FileSystemMgmt.grow). What was on the disks is lost, and the server checks nothing about them or the level: the interface offers this only for RAID5 and RAID6 arrays that are healthy and idle. Marks the mdadm and initramfs modules dirty (observed on the test VM). Returns the plugin's change record.

post.summary: Take a disk out of an array
post.description: Mark a member failed and take it out of the array, at once. Taking out a failed member or a spare loses nothing. Taking out a working member leaves the array with less protection, or none, and the server checks nothing about what is left: the interface itself refuses it while the array is short of a disk or busy, and for a level without copies. Nothing is erased: the disk keeps the array's marks, so it is not a candidate for anything until it is erased (DiskMgmt.wipe). Marks the mdadm and initramfs modules dirty (observed on the test VM). Returns the plugin's change record, whose `numdevices` is not the array's new count.

Stop an array and erase the array's marks from its member disks, at once. Everything stored on the array is lost and cannot be recovered. The server checks nothing about what is stored on it or what uses it; the interface itself refuses while a file system on it is set up, mounted, used or being created, or other storage uses it (`_used`). The system refuses to stop an array whose file system is mounted (HTTP 500, with mdadm's words). Marks the mdadm and initramfs modules dirty (observed on the test VM). Returns the plugin's change record.

500.description: The array could not be stopped, such as while its file system is mounted.

post.summary: Start or stop checking an array
post.description: Tell the kernel to check an array ("check": read every disk and compare the copies, for hours, changing nothing) or to stop a check ("idle"). Returns null at once; MdMgmt.enumerateDevices shows the check while it runs. A check wakes every disk of the array and keeps them busy. A level without copies (stripe) has nothing to check, and the call fails with HTTP 500. Changes no configuration, so nothing is pending afterwards.

500.description: The array has no copies to check, or there is no such array.

post.summary: File systems found but not set up
post.description: The detected file systems OMV could set up for mounting: not mounted, not on the system disk, not swap or bcache, and with no mount entry yet. A file system just created, and one from another computer, are among them. Each row is the same object as FileSystemMgmt.enumerateFilesystems returns, which this method calls, so reading it touches the disks no more than getList does. Changes nothing.

post.summary: Disks free for a new file system
post.description: The devices the server would offer for a new file system, as a background task, so a disk that hangs does not hold the request; the task's result is the list. It leaves out read-only devices, those that hold a file system or are part of one, and any that still carries a partition table or a file system, RAID or other signature. It reads that from the system's device information first and runs wipefs on a device only when that says nothing, which reads the disk. Changes nothing; the interface starts it only when the reader opens the add-storage flow or re-checks.

post.summary: Create a file system on a disk
post.description: Erase a device and create one file system across it, as a background task: the server removes the partition table and signatures, makes one partition over the whole disk (a RAID array or other stacked device is used as it is), and formats it. Everything on the device is lost and cannot be recovered. The server erases any device it is given: it does not check that the device is a candidate, empty, unmounted or not the system disk. Before calling it the interface itself refuses every device that its candidate list and the disk-use model do not both allow (journal, 2026-11-21). While it runs, FileSystemMgmt.getList shows the new file system as being created (status 2). The task's output is the commands' log text; it has no result. The new file system is neither mounted nor set up: FileSystemMgmt.setMountPoint does that. Changes no configuration, so nothing is pending afterwards.

post.summary: Combine disks into one BTRFS file system
post.description: Erase several disks and create one BTRFS file system across them, as a background task: the server removes each disk's partition table and signatures and runs mkfs.btrfs on the whole disks (no partitions). Everything on every disk is lost and cannot be recovered. The server erases any devices it is given and checks neither that they are candidates nor that there are enough for the profile; the interface refuses both itself (journal, 2026-11-21). Unlike FileSystemMgmt.create it leaves no "being created" row in FileSystemMgmt.getList while it runs. The task's output is mkfs.btrfs's text; it has no result. The new file system is neither mounted nor set up. Changes no configuration.

post.summary: Set up a file system for mounting
post.description: Create the mount entry of a file system found on a disk, with its warning level and tags. The server records it by a predictable device file (its /dev/disk/by-uuid/ link first) and makes its folder under /srv; it refuses a file system that already has a mount entry (HTTP 500). Nothing is mounted yet: it marks the fstab, collectd, monit and quota modules dirty (observed on the test VM), and applying fstab mounts it. Returns the stored mount entry.

500.description: The file system already has a mount entry, or it was not found.

post.summary: Grow a file system to fill its device
post.description: Grow a mounted file system to the full size of the device it is on, after that device has grown (a larger RAID array, say). This cannot be undone: nothing shrinks it again. It loses nothing, and the file system stays mounted and in use while it grows. Synchronous: the request lasts as long as the resize. The server refuses a type that cannot grow while mounted ("does not support online resizing"). When there is no room to grow it does nothing and still returns null (observed on the test VM). Changes no configuration.

500.description: The type cannot grow while mounted, or there is no such file system.

post.summary: Unmount a file system and forget it
post.description: Unmount the file system on a folder and delete its mount entry, with its warning level and tags. Nothing on the file system is deleted, but everything on it is out of reach until it is set up again. A file system in use (a program with a file open, or a shell in its folder) is refused with the system's "target is busy" message (HTTP 500), and then nothing changes. The server does not check what refers to the mount entry: it deletes the entry even while shared folders still point to it, so the interface refuses that itself (journal, 2026-11-21). It then applies the fstab module at once by itself, forced, which also applies any other mount change already pending and, like every apply, discards the snapshots that undoing pending changes restores from. It leaves the collectd, monit and quota modules dirty (observed on the test VM). Slow, because of that apply.

500.description: The file system is in use, or the folder has no mount entry.

post.description: The file system's own report on itself, as text. Its tools read the file system on the disk, so it can wake a sleeping disk: the interface reads it only when the reader asks. For BTRFS it works only while the file system is mounted; otherwise the server fails ("Failed to get mountpoint", observed on the test VM). Fails with HTTP 500 when the device holds no file system. Changes nothing.

500.description: The device holds no file system, or a BTRFS file system is not mounted.

post.description: The mount entry OMV has for a file system, found by its UUID or any of its device files, or the boolean false when it has none (this method does not fail for that). Reads only the configuration; touches no disk. Changes nothing.

post.summary: Save a file system's warning level and tags
post.description: Store a mount entry; the interface uses it only to change the warning level and the tags of an existing one. On a change it marks only the monit module dirty (observed on the test VM): the warning level takes effect when that is applied, and nothing is unmounted or mounted. Returns the stored entry.

post.summary: The compression names the plugin knows
post.description: A fixed list of compression names, from the plugin's source: it runs no command and reads nothing on the NAS, so the interface reads it once after an administrator signs in to learn whether the ZFS plugin is installed (design phase-5-zfs 0.11, P14); the list itself is not used. Changes nothing. When the plugin is not installed, OMV does not know the service and the call fails with HTTP 404 "RPC service 'Zfs' not found.".

404.description: The ZFS plugin is not installed: OMV knows no Zfs service. Code 0, message "RPC service 'Zfs' not found.".

post.description: Every pool, file system and volume in one flat list (ZfsObject), each pool twice: its pool row and its own folder. The server runs ZFS's status and list commands for every pool and its listing command for every file system and volume, and reads OMV's shared folders; on the test VM no member disk was read while it ran, also first after the pool was imported (journal). Changes nothing. The plugin does not check the paging parameters itself; it passes them to the backend's paging as getAllSnapshots does after checking them against rpc.common.getlist, so the contract holds them to that datamodel.

post.summary: ZFS's report on a pool or a file system
post.description: ZFS's own report as display text (ZfsReport): for a pool, zpool status with its device tree, error counts, the scan line of the last or running check or rebuild, and the damaged files; for a file system, its zfs list line and every property. It is the only reply that says what each disk is doing and how far a check or rebuild has got. The server runs ZFS's status or listing command; on the test VM no member disk was read while it ran (journal). Changes nothing. A pool or file system that does not exist fails with HTTP 500 and ZFS's words.

500.description: There is no such pool or file system.

post.description: Every disk of one pool from ZFS's structured status report, with its path, its state and the group it is in. The paths are those ZFS opened the disks by; the report (getObjectDetails) prints only their last part. The server runs ZFS's status command for the pool; on the test VM no member disk was read while it ran (journal). Changes nothing. A pool that does not exist, and a failure to ask ZFS, both answer an empty list, so the interface treats an empty list for a pool it has listed as a failed read (design phase-5-zfs 0.8, D10).

Every pool's name, state, error status and how full it is, from ZFS's status and list commands only (no file system is listed). On the test VM no member disk was read while it ran, also first after the pool was imported, so it may be read where no page about pools is open (design phase-5-zfs P14; journal). Changes nothing. An empty list means no pool, or that ZFS could not be asked; the plugin answers both the same way.

Every snapshot on every pool, with what it holds; not when it was taken. The server runs ZFS's listing command for every snapshot; on the test VM no member disk was read while it ran (journal). Changes nothing.

post.summary: Disks that can go into a pool
post.description: The disks the plugin offers for a new pool or as a replacement: not read-only, not connected by USB, not named by another service's settings, not in use, and with no file system or partition table found on them, each by its stable /dev/disk/by-id/ name. The disks of a deleted pool keep ZFS's partition table and are not offered until they are wiped (observed on the test VM). The server asks the system's device information and the configuration; on the test VM it read no pool's disk (journal). Changes nothing.

Erase the disks given and make them into a new pool of one group, at once, then turn its compression on and register its own folder (/<name>) with OMV as a file system. Every disk is overwritten and what was on it is lost; the server checks nothing about the disks itself, and ZFS refuses only a disk that holds a pool or a file system (HTTP 500), so the interface itself refuses every disk its candidate list and the disk-use model do not both allow (design phase-5-zfs 0.8). A "basic" pool has no protection: if one of its disks fails, everything on it is lost. A create ZFS refuses may still have written a partition table to the disks (observed on the test VM for a reserved name). Marks the fstab, collectd, monit and quota modules dirty (observed on the test VM).

500.description: ZFS refused: a disk is in use, or the name is one ZFS keeps for itself.

post.summary: Create a file system on a pool
post.description: Create a file system at the top of a pool, in its default folder (/<pool>/<name>), mount it and register it with OMV as a file system. It inherits the pool's compression. The plugin does not refuse a name that is taken: it answers as if it had created it and changes nothing (observed on the test VM), so the interface checks the name itself. Marks the fstab, collectd, monit and quota modules dirty (observed on the test VM).

post.summary: Set a file system's size limit or compression
post.description: Set a file system's size limit (quota) or compression, at once. A new compression applies to what is written from then on. ZFS refuses a limit below what the file system holds (HTTP 500), and then nothing changes. Marks the collectd, monit and quota modules dirty (observed on the test VM).

500.description: ZFS refused the value, such as a size limit below what the file system holds.

post.description: Take a snapshot of a file system (with recursive, of the file systems inside it too), named by the NAS's date and time to the second ("YYYY-MM-DD_hh-mm-ss"). A second snapshot of the same file system in the same second is refused (HTTP 500), as its name is taken. Marks nothing dirty (observed on the test VM).

500.description: ZFS refused, such as a second snapshot in the same second.

post.summary: Roll a file system back to a snapshot
post.description: Put a file system back as it was when the snapshot was taken, at once. Every change made since is lost and cannot be recovered. ZFS refuses when newer snapshots exist (HTTP 500), and then nothing changes; the contract has no way to ask it to delete them. Marks nothing dirty (observed on the test VM).

500.description: ZFS refused, such as a snapshot with newer snapshots after it.

post.summary: Delete a snapshot, a file system or a pool
post.description: Delete, as a background task: a snapshot; a file system with everything in it, all its snapshots and its mount entry; or a pool, destroying it and clearing ZFS's marks from its partitions (the disks keep ZFS's partition table). Everything deleted is lost and cannot be recovered. Also removes the plugin's scheduled jobs that name it. The plugin refuses (the task fails with HTTP 500 and its words) a file system with file systems inside it, a pool that holds any file system or volume, and either while a shared folder uses it; the interface checks all of these itself first (design phase-5-zfs 0.10). The task's output is empty; it has no result. Marks the fstab, collectd, monit and quota modules dirty, for a snapshot too (observed on the test VM).

Start a check (scrub) of a pool, or continue a paused one: ZFS reads every disk of the pool in full and repairs what it can from a copy: seconds on the test VM's small disks, hours on large ones. The check runs in ZFS, not as a task; getObjectDetails shows how far it has got. Marks nothing dirty (observed on the test VM).
Stop a pool's check, running or paused. Nothing on the pool changes; a later check starts from the beginning. With no check in progress ZFS refuses (HTTP 500). Marks nothing dirty.

500.description: There is no check to stop.

post.summary: Replace a disk of a pool
post.description: Put a new disk in place of a disk of the pool, at once: ZFS erases the new disk and rebuilds onto it (resilvering) in the background, and takes the old disk out of the pool when the rebuild ends. Everything on the new disk is lost. The old disk keeps ZFS's marks and is not offered as a candidate until it is wiped (observed on the test VM). The rebuild runs in ZFS, not as a task; getObjectDetails shows it. Marks nothing dirty (observed on the test VM).

post.summary: Take a disk of a pool offline
post.description: Make ZFS stop using a disk until it is brought back, at once: the pool keeps working on its other disks, without the protection that disk gave (DEGRADED). ZFS refuses when no copy of the data would be left (HTTP 500). Marks nothing dirty (observed on the test VM).

500.description: ZFS refused, such as the last disk that holds a copy.

post.description: Bring a disk taken offline back into use; ZFS copies onto it what changed meanwhile. The plugin hands ZFS the whole disk for a partition path it is given. Marks nothing dirty (observed on the test VM).

Set the read, write and checksum error counts of a pool's disks back to zero, and let ZFS try a failed disk again. Nothing on the pool changes, but the record of the errors is gone. Marks nothing dirty.

ConfigAppliedModules.description: The result of an apply task (its final output, parsed as JSON) - the modules deployed.

SmartDeviceList.description: The result of the S.M.A.R.T. list task (its final output, parsed as JSON): the disks that support S.M.A.R.T., paged, sorted and searched by the backend.

FilesystemCandidateList.description: The devices the server offers for a new file system, in no particular order. A disk that holds anything, even an empty partition table, is left out without a word.

Username.description: An account name, in OMV's `username` format.

Role.description: The session's role. `admin` is an administrator; anything else is treated as a user.

SessionAuthenticated.description: A signed-in session. The server also sends `sessionid`; the transport ignores it and it is not described here (UI-6). The session lives in OMV's HttpOnly cookie.

SessionChallengeRequired.description: The password was right and a second factor is required. The interface shows its own screen for each `kind` it knows (A10). The server also sends `challenge.redirecturl`, a route of the stock interface; it is ignored and not described here (UI-3). No other call may be made before Session.verify: any call discards the pending challenge.

kind.description: The second-factor method, e.g. `totp`. An unknown kind sends the user to the classic interface.

RpcErrorDetail.description: The `error` member of an rpc.php failure reply. The transport turns it into an RpcError with the HTTP status; its `trace` is discarded at once and never described here (UI-9). `code` is 0 for every error observed (A8), so the status and the message are the only signals.

message.description: The backend's message, already translated by the server. Shown as text.

SessionVerifyRequest.description: The answer to a `totp` challenge (openmediavault-2fa-totp, A10). OMV's core accepts any value here and hands it to the two-factor plugin; the contract accepts only the one shape the interface sends.

SystemInformation.description: System information. Every signed-in user gets `ts`, `time` and `hostname`; an administrator also gets the rest.

ts.description: Unix time on the server, in seconds.

time.description: Display text, the server's local time in the server's locale.

memUtilization.description: A fraction from 0 to 1, as a decimal string (A4).

dirtyModules.description: Module name to the module's description (display text). An empty map arrives as `[]`; the transport turns it into `{}`.

modules.description: Ask about these modules only. Empty or absent asks about every module.
The modules to deploy. Empty deploys every dirty module.

force.description: Deploy the listed modules even if they are not dirty; with no modules, every module.

TaskHandle.description: A background task handle: the server path of the task's status file. Opaque. Held in memory only, never shown, never put in a URL or storage, and passed to Exec only by the task helper (UI-5).

filename.description: Always empty, as the stock interface sends; the server finds the revision itself.

pos.description: Byte offset to read from; the `pos` of the previous reply.

ExecOutput.description: New output of a task since `pos`. The poll that reports `running: false` with nothing pending is the last one: the server then deletes the task, and any further call on the handle fails (A6). A failed task makes this call itself fail, with the task's output as the message.

output.description: Plain text since the requested position, line endings normalised to newlines.

extraoptions.description: Extra lines for the SSH server's configuration file. Free text.

GetListRequest.description: Paging, sorting and search for a list (rpc.common.getlist). The backend sorts and searches the whole list. `limit` null returns every row (A2). OMV also accepts an integer `search`; the contract accepts text only.

perms.description: 0 no access, 5 read-only, 7 read and write.

SharedFolder.description: A shared folder (conf.system.sharedfolder) with the fields ShareMgmt computes.

mntentref.description: The UUID of the file system's mount point.

reldirpath.description: The folder's path inside its file system.

privileges.description: The privileges set on the folder; the empty string when none are set (observed).

_used.description: True if another configuration object refers to this folder.

device.description: The file system's label, else its device file; empty if unknown.

description.description: Display text built by the server.

status.description: OK, or why the folder cannot be reached: ENOTDIR, ENOENT or ENOENT_DB_MNTENT in OMV 8.6. Open to other codes, so a later OMV's code is shown as Unknown rather than refused.

ShareCandidate.description: A file system that can hold a new shared folder: mounted now, not a bind mount, and of a type that can hold one (ShareMgmt.getCandidates).

uuid.description: The UUID of the file system's mount entry, which ShareMgmt.set takes as `mntentref`.

description.description: Display text built by the server in English: the device and the file system's tags, or the file system's own description. Not shown.

ShareCandidateList.description: The file systems that can hold a new shared folder, in the server's order.

ObjectUuid.description: A configuration object's UUID, in OMV's `uuidv4` format. To create an object, send OMV's placeholder for an object not yet saved, fa4b1c66-ef79-11e5-87a0-0002b3a176b4; the server gives the new object its own UUID and returns it.

SharedFolderName.description: A shared folder's name, in OMV's `sharename` format: 1 to 80 bytes (OMV counts bytes in UTF-8, so a name in another script holds fewer letters), none of " \ / [ ] : | < > + = ; , * ?, no control character, no space at the start or end. The contract keeps OMV's rule so that a folder made elsewhere (named `homes`, say) can be written back with its description changed; a NEW name is held to the interface's stricter rules before it is sent (design phase-5-shares 0.5: no leading full stop, no two in a row, not a name Samba keeps for itself, unique ignoring case).

SharedFolderRelPath.description: The folder a shared folder uses, inside its file system: "/" for the whole file system, or a path without a leading "/"; a trailing "/" is allowed, as OMV stores it, so a row read from ShareMgmt.getList can be sent back. Stricter than OMV: never empty, never two full stops anywhere (OMV refuses them too), no control character and no "\". A NEW path is held to the interface's stricter rules before it is sent (design phase-5-shares 0.5: at most eight folders, none starting with a full stop).

ShareMgmtSetRequest.description: A shared folder to store (rpc.sharemgmt.set). With OMV's placeholder UUID it makes a new one, and makes its folder on the disk at once if it does not exist; otherwise it rewrites the stored one, keeping its access list. Stricter than OMV: the path rules of SharedFolderRelPath, a description of at most 255 characters, and the file mode only "770" (design phase-5-shares P4), which OMV applies only to a folder it makes. A new name and path are also held to the interface's own rules (design 0.5) before they are sent.

comment.description: The description, shown in lists only; may be empty.

mntentref.description: The UUID of the file system's mount entry, from ShareMgmt.getCandidates.

mode.description: The new folder's file permissions: the owner and the group every person belongs to may read and write, nobody else. Applied only when OMV makes the folder.

SharedFolderSaved.description: The stored shared folder (conf.system.sharedfolder) as ShareMgmt.set or ShareMgmt.delete returns it, without the fields ShareMgmt.getList computes.

uuid.description: The folder's UUID; for a new folder, the one the server gave it.

reldirpath.description: The folder's path inside its file system, with a trailing "/".

mode.description: The file mode ShareMgmt.set applied, or would have applied, to a folder it made.

SharedFolderPrivilegeEntry.description: One entry of a shared folder's access list, as ShareMgmt.setPrivileges takes it.

perms.description: 7 read and write, 5 read only, 0 refused even through a group (only while guest access is off). The interface stores no entry for "No access" and keeps a 0 it read (design 0.4).

ShareMgmtSetPrivilegesRequest.description: A shared folder's whole access list (rpc.sharemgmt.setprivileges). It replaces the stored list: an entry left out is removed. Stricter than OMV: `privileges` is required (OMV does not mark it) and holds at most 10,000 entries.

ShareMgmtDeleteRequest.description: A shared folder to delete (rpc.sharemgmt.delete). `recursive` false removes only the shared folder's record and leaves every file on the disk; `recursive` true first deletes its folder on the disk and everything in it, inside the request.

UserMgmtGetUserListRequest.description: Paging, sorting and search for the list of people (rpc.usermgmt.getuserlist). `limit` null returns every row. Stricter than OMV: `detail` only "basic", and `search` text only.

UserAccount.description: A person's account that is not a system account (UserMgmt.getUserList), with what OMV stores about it. The interface shows only the name and the description.

comment.description: The account's description; may be empty.

groups.description: The names of the groups the person belongs to, their primary group included.

UserGroup.description: A group that is not a system group (UserMgmt.getGroupList). `comment` is present only when OMV holds a record for the group.

members.description: The names of the people in it as members (not those for whom it is the primary group).

SmbSettings.description: The SMB/CIFS service's settings without its shares (SMB.getSettings, conf.service.smb). The interface changes only `enable` and sends everything else back as read (design 0.10).

enable.description: Whether Windows and Mac sharing is on for the whole NAS.

SmbSetSettingsRequest.description: The SMB/CIFS service's settings to store (rpc.smb.setsettings). OMV writes the fields sent over the stored object and keeps the rest; the interface always sends the whole SMB.getSettings reply with only `enable` changed. The twelve fields OMV's datamodel requires are required; the stored home-folder, `netbios` and `minprotocol` fields, which OMV's datamodel does not name but stores when sent, are optional and within the bounds of conf.service.smb. With `enable` true OMV refuses a NAS name longer than 15 characters, and home-folder sharing while home folders are off.

SmbShare.description: An SMB share as stored (conf.service.smb.share): one shared folder reached from Windows and Mac computers. OMV allows at most one per shared folder.

enable.description: False when it was turned off for this folder.

sharedfolderref.description: The UUID of the shared folder it shares.

guest.description: no: only people given access; allow: anyone on the network too, without a password; only: everyone who opens it is treated as a guest. Open to other values from a later OMV.

SmbShareRow.description: An SMB share as SMB.getShareList lists it, with the name of its shared folder.

sharedfoldername.description: The shared folder's name, which is also the share's name on the network.

SmbSetShareRequest.description: An SMB share to store (rpc.smb.setshare). OMV builds a fresh object from what is sent, so a field left out returns to its default: the interface sends a share read from SMB.getShareList without `sharedfoldername`, with only the fields it changes (design 0.10), or for a new share the classic form's defaults. Every field OMV's datamodel requires is required. The stored fields OMV's datamodel does not name (`macoscompat`, `timemachinemaxsize`, `transportencryption`, `followsymlinks`, `widelinks`) are accepted and stored, so they are optional here, within the bounds of conf.service.smb.share. OMV refuses a second share for the same shared folder.

guest.description: The interface chooses "no" or "allow"; "only" is accepted so a share set to it in the classic interface keeps it until the reader changes it.

ObjectUuidRequest.description: One configuration object, by its UUID (rpc.common.objectuuid).

items.description: A public key in RFC 4716 format.

_readonly.description: True if the administrator does not let this user change their account.

AutoLogoutSettings.description: The session timeout, from the web administration settings (conf.webadmin). The server ends a session that has been idle this long.

timeout.description: Minutes. 0 means the server never ends an idle session.

enablessl.description: Whether the web interface is also served over HTTPS.

forcesslonly.description: Whether HTTP is redirected to HTTPS.

sslcertificateref.description: The UUID of the certificate used for HTTPS, or empty when none is chosen.

timeout.description: Minutes an idle session lasts. 0 means the server never ends an idle session.

Email.description: An e-mail address, in OMV's `email` format. OMV checks it with PHP's FILTER_VALIDATE_EMAIL; this pattern accepts a subset of that: a dot-atom local part of at most 64 characters, and a domain of two or more labels whose last starts with a letter. Quoted local parts and address literals, which PHP also accepts, are refused.

UserMgmtSetUserByContextRequest.description: The signed-in user's own e-mail address and description (rpc.usermgmt.setuserbycontext). OMV also accepts `password` here; the contract leaves it out, because the interface changes a password only through UserMgmt.setPasswordByContext.

comment.description: The account's description. The system's account tools refuse a colon or a line break, so the contract does too.

UserByContextSaved.description: The account as UserMgmt.setUserByContext stored it. The server also echoes the password that was submitted (always empty, since the contract does not send one); the contract leaves it out and the transport removes it from the reply (`x-omv-omit`).

disallowusermod.description: True if the administrator does not let this user change their account.

items.description: A public key in RFC 4716 format.

UserMgmtSetPasswordByContextRequest.description: The signed-in user's new password (rpc.usermgmt.setpasswordbycontext). OMV accepts an empty password; the contract does not.

NetworkGeneralSettings.description: The host name and domain name of the system (conf.system.network.dns).

hostname.description: The host name, without the domain.

domainname.description: The domain name, or empty when none is set.

TimeSettings.description: The system clock and time settings (conf.system.time), with the server's current date added by the method.

date.description: The server's date and time when the method ran.

local.description: Display text, the server's local time in the server's locale.

ISO8601.description: The same moment in ISO 8601, with the server's offset from UTC.

timezone.description: The time zone name, e.g. "Etc/UTC" or "Europe/Berlin".

ntpenable.description: Whether the clock is set from time servers.

ntptimeservers.description: The time servers, as one string as OMV stores it.

ntpclients.description: The networks allowed to use this system as a time server, as OMV stores them.

EmailNotificationSettings.description: How the system sends notification e-mail (conf.system.notification.email). The server also sends the SMTP password in plain text; the contract leaves it out and the transport removes it from the reply before anything else sees it (`x-omv-omit` on EmailNotification.get).

enable.description: Whether notifications are sent by e-mail.

server.description: The SMTP server's name or address, or empty.

tls.description: How the connection to the SMTP server is encrypted.

sender.description: The sender's e-mail address, or empty.

primaryemail.description: The address notifications go to, or empty.

secondaryemail.description: A second address notifications go to, or empty.

authenable.description: Whether the system signs in to the SMTP server.

username.description: The user name for the SMTP server, or empty.

FileSystemMgmtEnumerateMountedFilesystem.description: Which mounted file systems to list (rpc.filesystemmgmt.enumeratemountedfilesystems). Both fields are optional.

type.description: Only file systems of this type, such as "ext4".

includeroot.description: Also list the file system the system runs from, mounted at "/". Defaults to false. Its row is made up by the server, with a warning threshold from the server's environment (85 by default).

MountedFilesystem.description: A file system that is configured and mounted now. A configured file system whose disk is missing or that is not mounted is left out of the list without a word; bind mounts are left out too. A ZFS file system (type "zfs", from the openmediavault-zfs plugin) has its full name ("tank/media") as its device files and label, no UUID (null) and no devlinks, and its sizes as JSON numbers (observed on the test VM).

devicename.description: The kernel's name for the partition or device, such as "sda1".

devicefile.description: The device file OMV prefers, usually a /dev/disk/by-uuid/ link.

canonicaldevicefile.description: The device file under /dev, such as "/dev/sda1".

parentdevicefile.description: The disk the file system is on, such as "/dev/sda".

uuid.description: The file system's own UUID (not a configuration object's). Null for a ZFS file system, which has none (observed on the test VM).

type.description: The file system type, such as "ext4" or "btrfs".

mountpoint.description: The configured mount point, such as "/srv/dev-disk-by-uuid-...".

blocks.description: Size in 1 KiB blocks. "-1" when the server could not read the usage. A ZFS file system sends a JSON number, its size divided by 1024, which may have a fraction (read from the plugin's source); the transport turns a whole number into its decimal string.

size.description: Bytes. "-1" when the server could not read the usage. A ZFS file system sends a JSON number, which the transport turns into its decimal string.

available.description: Bytes free. "-1" when the server could not read the usage. A ZFS file system sends a JSON number, which the transport turns into its decimal string; it is the pool's free space, shared with the other file systems on the pool.

used.description: Display text, such as "12.34 GiB": the server formats it, unlike size and available, which are bytes. "-1" when the server could not read the usage.

percentage.description: Percent used. -1 when the server could not read the usage.

description.description: Display text, such as "/dev/sda1 [EXT4, 2.03 MiB (1%) used, 7.75 GiB available]".

usagewarnthreshold.description: Percent used at which OMV warns about this file system. 0 means it never warns.

MountedFilesystemList.description: Every mounted file system, in no particular order. A plain list: not paged, and without the {total, data} wrapper of the list methods.

ConfiguredFilesystem.description: A file system configured in OMV, or one being created, with its state in `status`. A configured file system that is not detected (status 3) or still being created (status 2) has no usage: its sizes are "-1", its percentage -1 and most device fields empty. A ZFS file system (type "zfs", from the openmediavault-zfs plugin) has its full name ("tank/media") as devicename, devicefile, predictabledevicefile, canonicaldevicefile and label, no UUID (null), no devlinks, its pool's disks as devicefiles and the first of them as parentdevicefile, and its sizes as JSON numbers (observed on the test VM).

status.description: 1 available (detected, and online when mounted), 2 being created, 3 missing (configured but not detected: its disk may be disconnected or have failed).

devicename.description: The kernel's name for the partition or device, such as "sda1"; empty unless available.

devicefile.description: The device file OMV prefers. For a missing file system, the configured device file, or empty when it was configured by UUID.

uuid.description: The file system's own UUID. For a missing file system, the configured UUID, or empty when it was configured by device file. Null for a ZFS file system, which has none (observed on the test VM).

label.description: The file system's label; empty when it has none, null for one being created (observed).

type.description: The file system type, such as "ext4" or "btrfs".

mountpoint.description: The configured mount point; empty for a file system being created.

blocks.description: Size in 1 KiB blocks. "-1" when there is no reading. A ZFS file system sends a JSON number, its size divided by 1024, which may have a fraction (read from the plugin's source); the transport turns a whole number into its decimal string.

size.description: Bytes. "-1" when there is no reading. A ZFS file system sends a JSON number (used plus available), which the transport turns into its decimal string.

available.description: Bytes free. "-1" when there is no reading. A ZFS file system sends a JSON number, which the transport turns into its decimal string; it is the pool's free space, shared with the other file systems on the pool.

used.description: Display text, such as "12.34 GiB". "-1" when there is no reading.

percentage.description: Percent used. -1 when there is no reading.

hasmultipledevices.description: Whether it spans several devices; the empty string unless available (read from source).

usagewarnthreshold.description: Percent used at which OMV warns; 0 means it never warns. Absent for a file system being created.

mountopts.description: The configured mount options. Absent for a file system being created.

_used.description: Whether something (a shared folder, for one) refers to this file system.

total.description: Every matching file system, before paging.

DetectedFilesystem.description: A file system the system detects on a disk, partition or other block device, whether or not OMV has set it up: the system's own root and boot file systems, swap space, and file systems from another computer included. A file system that is not mounted has no usage: its sizes are "-1" and its percentage -1. A ZFS file system (type "zfs", from the openmediavault-zfs plugin) is found by the plugin, not by blkid: its full name ("tank/media") stands for its device files and label, it has no UUID (null) and no devlinks, its pool's disks are its devicefiles, and its sizes are JSON numbers (observed on the test VM).

devicename.description: The kernel's name for the partition or device, such as "sda1".

devicefile.description: The device file OMV prefers, usually a /dev/disk/by-uuid/ link.

canonicaldevicefile.description: The device file under /dev, such as "/dev/sda1".

parentdevicefile.description: The device the file system is on, under /dev: the disk of a partition ("/dev/sda" for "/dev/sda1"), or the device itself when it has no partitions.

uuid.description: The file system's own identifier: a UUID for most types, a short volume ID for FAT ("ABCD-1234" form), a date-like value for an optical disc. Null for a ZFS file system, which has none (observed on the test VM).

type.description: The file system type as blkid reports it, such as "ext4", "btrfs", "vfat", "iso9660", or "swap" for swap space.

mounted.description: Whether it is mounted now. Swap space in use is never reported as mounted.

mountpoint.description: Where it is mounted, such as "/" or "/boot/efi"; empty when it is not mounted.

blocks.description: Size in 1 KiB blocks. "-1" when not mounted. A ZFS file system sends a JSON number, its size divided by 1024, which may have a fraction (read from the plugin's source); the transport turns a whole number into its decimal string.

size.description: Bytes. "-1" when not mounted. A ZFS file system sends a JSON number, which the transport turns into its decimal string.

available.description: Bytes free. "-1" when not mounted. A ZFS file system sends a JSON number, which the transport turns into its decimal string.

used.description: Display text, such as "12.34 GiB". "-1" when not mounted.

description.description: Display text, such as "/dev/sda1 [EXT4, 2.03 MiB (1%) used, 7.75 GiB available]".

hasmultipledevices.description: Whether it spans several devices (btrfs across disks, for one).

devicefiles.description: Every device the file system is on, under /dev, such as ["/dev/sda1"].

_readonly.description: True for the file system the system runs from.

_used.description: Whether OMV has set it up and something (a shared folder, for one) refers to it; always true for the file system the system runs from.

DetectedFilesystemList.description: Every file system the system detects, in no particular order.

ServiceStatus.description: One service whose state OMV reports. Plugins add their own services to the list.

name.description: The OMV module's name, such as "samba" or "ssh".

title.description: Display text, translated by the server, such as "SMB/CIFS".

enabled.description: Whether the service is turned on in OMV's settings.

running.description: Whether systemd reports the service active now.

ServiceStatusList.description: Every service whose state OMV reports, in no particular order. Not paged.

ServiceStatsText.description: Display text: the raw output of the service's status commands, in the server's language, shown as preformatted text. When the service is turned off, the text "Service disabled", translated by the server.

NetworkDeviceStats.description: The interface's counters since the system started, from /proc/net/dev, each a whole number as text. The server sends [] (PHP's empty map) when it cannot read them.

NetworkDevice.description: A network interface the system has, with its addresses, link and counters, and, when it is configured in OMV, the fields of its configuration (conf.system.network.interface). The loopback interface "lo" is included.

uuid.description: The interface's configuration object, or OMV's placeholder for an object not yet saved (fa4b1c66-ef79-11e5-87a0-0002b3a176b4) when it is not configured in OMV.

devicename.description: The kernel's name for the interface, such as "enp2s0" or "lo".

type.description: ethernet, wifi, vlan, bond, bridge, virtual, loopback or unknown; absent for some interfaces. Open to other values.

method.description: How IPv4 is configured, such as "dhcp" or "static". Only for a configured interface.

method6.description: How IPv6 is configured. Only for a configured interface.

address.description: The IPv4 address; the empty string when it has none.

netmask.description: The IPv4 netmask; the empty string when it has none.

prefix.description: The IPv4 prefix length; -1 when it has no address.

address6.description: The IPv6 address; the empty string when it has none.

prefix6.description: The IPv6 prefix length; -1 when it has no address.

state.description: The kernel's operational state: UP, DOWN, LOWERLAYERDOWN, NOTPRESENT, TESTING, DORMANT or UNKNOWN (the loopback interface reports UNKNOWN). Open to other values.

link.description: Whether the interface has a link.

vlanid.description: The VLAN ID; -1 when the interface is not a VLAN.

speed.description: Mbit/s; -1 when unknown (the loopback interface, a link that is down).

description.description: Display text, the name and MAC address, such as "enp2s0 [00:00:5e:00:53:01]".

wpassid.description: The Wi-Fi network name. Only for a configured Wi-Fi interface.

LogFileGetListRequest.description: Which log to read, and a page of it (rpc.logfile.getlist). The server re-reads and parses the whole log, up to its last 100000 lines, on every call, whatever page is asked for. `search` is not in OMV's datamodel, but the method reads it: a case-insensitive search over every column.

limit.description: The number of rows; null returns every row.

id.description: The log, such as syslog, auth, boot, daemon, messages, dmesg, rsync, rsyncd, smartd, apt_term or smbdaudit. Plugins add more. An unknown id fails.

LogRow.description: One line of a log, parsed. Every row has `rownum`; the other columns depend on the log. Journal logs (syslog, auth, daemon, boot, ...) have ts, date, hostname and message; some file logs only message; the SMB/CIFS audit log (smbdaudit) has its own columns, listed here. Plugins' logs may have others.

rownum.description: The line's place in the part of the log read, from 0.

ts.description: Unix time of the line, in seconds; null when the server could not read its time.

date.description: Display text, the line's time in the server's locale. Not for parsing.

message.description: The line's text. Shown as text.

username.description: smbdaudit only. The user who did it.

clientnetbiosname.description: smbdaudit only. The client's NetBIOS name.

servicerootdir.description: smbdaudit only. The shared folder's path on the server.

operation.description: smbdaudit only. What was done, such as "openat", "unlinkat" or "renameat".

result.description: smbdaudit only. "ok", or "fail" with the reason.

filepath.description: smbdaudit only. The file's path, as Samba logged it.

filename.description: smbdaudit only. The last part of filepath.

total.description: Every matching row of the part of the log read, before paging.

SystemGetTopInfoRequest.description: The reply's form (rpc.system.gettopinfo). OMV also offers "text", top's output as one string; the contract asks only for "json", the parsed form.

TopProcess.description: One process as top lists it. Every value is text, as top prints it (jc --raw), except that the server turns VIRT, RES and SHR into bytes.

PR.description: The scheduling priority; "rt" for a real-time process.

S.description: The state: R running, S sleeping, D waiting for a disk, I idle, T stopped, t stopped by a debugger, Z zombie.

%CPU.description: Percent of one CPU since top's last update, such as "4.8".

TIME+.description: Display text, the CPU time used, such as "1:06.40".

TopInfo.description: A snapshot of top (top -b -n 1), parsed by jc. Every value is text, as top prints it. The memory and swap figures are in top's unit, MiB unless top is set otherwise. The server takes about a second to answer.

time.description: Display text, the server's local time, such as "03:27:44".

cpu_user.description: Percent of CPU time, such as "4.8"; the other cpu_ fields likewise.

HdParm.description: A disk's stored power and cache settings (conf.system.hdparm). They take effect when the pending changes are applied.

devicefile.description: The disk's /dev/disk/by-id/ link where it has one, otherwise the device file sent.

aam.description: Advanced Acoustic Management; 0 is off, 128 quiet, 254 fast.

spindowntime.description: The standby timer in the drive's encoding; 0 is never.

DiskDevice.description: A disk the system can see, including read-only ones such as an optical drive. Read without waking a disk that is in standby. `hdparm` is sent by DiskMgmt.getList only, and only for a disk with stored power and cache settings.

devicename.description: The kernel's name for the disk, such as "sda".

canonicaldevicefile.description: The device file under /dev, such as "/dev/sda".

devicefile.description: The disk's /dev/disk/by-id/ link where it has one, otherwise its device file.

description.description: Display text, such as "VMware Virtual SATA Hard Drive [/dev/sda, 8.00 GiB]".

wwn.description: The disk's World Wide Name; the empty string when it has none.

israid.description: Whether this is a hardware RAID device.

isroot.description: Whether the system is installed on this disk.

isreadonly.description: Whether the disk cannot be written to, such as an optical drive.

powermode.description: As smartctl reports it: "ACTIVE or IDLE", "ACTIVE", "IDLE", "STANDBY" (spun down) or "SLEEP"; "UNKNOWN" for a disk that does not support S.M.A.R.T. or does not report it (observed for an NVMe disk), and "ERROR" when it could not be read. Open to other values.

temperature.description: Degrees Celsius as text, such as "30". The empty string when unknown, and always for a disk in standby, which is not woken to read it. Also accepted as a whole number, the form the S.M.A.R.T. list was observed to send.

DiskDevices.description: Every disk the system can see, in no particular order.

DiskDeviceList.description: Every disk the system can see, each with its stored power and cache settings when it has any; paged and sorted by the backend.

DeviceFile.description: A device file, in OMV's `devicefile` format: a path under /dev, such as "/dev/sda" or a /dev/disk/by-id/ link. The server resolves it to the disk and fails when no such disk exists.

DiskMgmtSetHdParmRequest.description: A disk's power and cache settings (rpc.diskmgmt.sethdparm). Every field is required. The contract takes the stricter bound of the method's datamodel and the stored object's (conf.system.hdparm), which the server also checks: `apm` at most 254 and `spindowntime` at most 254.

apm.description: Advanced Power Management, 0 to turn it off, otherwise 1 (lowest power, the disk may spin down) to 254 (highest performance). From 128 up the disk does not spin down. The stock form offers 0, 1, 64, 127, 128, 192 and 254.

aam.description: Advanced Acoustic Management. 0 off, 128 quietest and slowest, 254 loudest and fastest.

spindowntime.description: The standby timer in the drive's own encoding, 0 for never: 1 to 240 count steps of 5 seconds (60 is 5 minutes, 240 is 20 minutes); 241 to 251 count steps of 30 minutes (241 is 30 minutes, 242 is 1 hour). The stock form offers 0, 60, 120, 240 and from 241 up.

writecache.description: Whether the disk's write cache is on.

DiskMgmtWipeRequest.description: The disk to wipe and how (rpc.diskmgmt.wipe). Both fields are required.

secure.description: false: a quick wipe, which removes the partition table and file system signatures in seconds. true: a secure wipe, which overwrites the whole disk once and can take hours.

SmartEnumeratedDevice.description: A disk that OMV can read S.M.A.R.T. data from, with its health as smartctl reports it. The model and serial number are smartctl's where it gives them.

temperature.description: Degrees Celsius, as text or a whole number; the empty string when unknown.

overallstatus.description: The disk's health, with the meanings of SmartDevice's `overallstatus`: GOOD, BAD_ATTRIBUTE_IN_THE_PAST, BAD_SECTOR, BAD_ATTRIBUTE_NOW, BAD_SECTOR_MANY or BAD_STATUS. Open to other values.

SmartEnumeratedDevices.description: Disks that OMV can read S.M.A.R.T. data from, in no particular order.

SmartSettings.description: The S.M.A.R.T. monitoring settings for every disk (conf.service.smartmontools). They take effect when the pending changes are applied.

powermode.description: Which disks a check skips so as not to wake them; never, sleep, standby or idle.

tempdiff.description: Report a temperature change of at least this many degrees Celsius; 0 is off.

tempmax.description: Report a temperature of at least this many degrees Celsius; 0 is off.

SmartSetSettingsRequest.description: The S.M.A.R.T. monitoring settings for every disk (rpc.smart.setsettings). Every field is required. `tempdiff` and `tempmax` take the stored object's maximum of 255 (conf.service.smartmontools), which the server also checks.

enable.description: Whether S.M.A.R.T. monitoring runs at all.

powermode.description: Which disks a check skips so that it does not wake them: never (checks every disk, waking it), sleep (skips disks in sleep mode), standby (skips disks in standby or sleep) or idle (skips disks that are idle, in standby or asleep).

tempdiff.description: Report a temperature change of at least this many degrees Celsius. 0 turns it off.

tempmax.description: Report a temperature of at least this many degrees Celsius. 0 turns it off.

DeviceFileRequest.description: One disk, by its device file (rpc.common.devicefile).

SmartDeviceSettings.description: One disk's stored S.M.A.R.T. monitoring settings (conf.service.smartmontools.device). They take effect when the pending changes are applied.

devicefile.description: The disk's /dev/disk/by-id/ link where it has one.

devicetype.description: The smartctl device type the server chose for the disk, such as "nvme"; may be empty.

tempdiff.description: 0 uses the setting for every disk.

tempmax.description: 0 uses the setting for every disk.
