_used.description: Smart.getDeviceSettings only: whether a scheduled self-test refers to this disk. The stock interface does not let monitoring be turned off while one does.

SmartSetDeviceSettingsRequest.description: One disk's S.M.A.R.T. monitoring settings (rpc.smart.setdevicesettings). The datamodel requires only `devicefile` and `enable` and does not declare `tempdiff` or `tempmax`, but the method reads all three of `uuid`, `tempdiff` and `tempmax` and stores them, so the contract requires them. The temperature limits take the stored object's bounds (conf.service.smartmontools.device).

tempdiff.description: Report a temperature change of at least this many degrees Celsius; 0 uses the setting for every disk. The stock form offers 0 to 15.

tempmax.description: Report a temperature of at least this many degrees Celsius; 0 uses the setting for every disk. The stock form offers 0 and 5 to 80 in steps of 5.

SmartInformation.description: What smartctl reports about one disk, as display text: each "Name: value" line of its information and S.M.A.R.T. data sections, keyed by the name in lower case with spaces and hyphens removed ("Device Model" becomes `devicemodel`). Which keys appear depends on the disk; the six required ones are always there, possibly empty. When smartctl repeats a name, the last line wins.

usercapacity.description: Display text, such as "8,589,934,592 bytes [8.58 GB]"; empty for an NVMe disk.

smartsupportis.description: Display text, such as "Enabled", or "Unavailable - device lacks SMART capability." (observed for the test VM's virtual SATA disks).

temperature.description: Degrees Celsius as text, such as "30"; absent when unknown.

powercycles.description: How often the disk was switched on, as text; absent when unknown.

poweronhours.description: Hours switched on, as text; absent when unknown. Some disks add minutes, such as "1234h+05m".

SmartAttribute.description: One S.M.A.R.T. attribute of an ATA disk, with OMV's assessment of it. `value`, `worst` and `threshold` are the drive's normalised values, where lower is worse.

flags.description: smartctl's flag letters, such as "PO--CK"; P marks a pre-failure attribute.

whenfailed.description: "-" when it never failed; otherwise "FAILING_NOW" or "In_the_past".

rawvalue.description: The raw value as smartctl prints it, such as "0" or "34 (Min/Max 19/46)".

description.description: Display text in English, written by the server; empty for an attribute it does not know.

prefailure.description: Whether a failure of this attribute predicts a failing disk.

assessment.description: OMV's assessment: GOOD, BAD_ATTRIBUTE_NOW (at or below its threshold now, or for Reported_Uncorrect any count), BAD_ATTRIBUTE_IN_THE_PAST (was at or below it) or BAD_SECTOR (reallocated or pending sectors). Open to other values.

SmartAttributeList.description: The disk's S.M.A.R.T. attributes, in smartctl's order. Empty for disks that report none in this form, such as NVMe and SAS disks and disks without S.M.A.R.T.

SmartSelfTestLogEntry.description: One entry of an ATA disk's self-test log, newest first. Every field is text as smartctl prints it.

num.description: The entry's number, "1" for the newest.

status.description: Display text, such as "Completed without error" or "Completed: read failure". It can end in spaces, which are smartctl's column padding.

remaining.description: Percent of the test left when it ended, such as "00" or "90".

lifetime.description: The disk's power-on hours when the test ran.

lbaoffirsterror.description: The first block that failed, or "-".

SmartSelfTestLog.description: The disk's self-test log. Only short and extended tests are listed; conveyance and other tests are left out, and NVMe disks report none in this form.

SmartExtendedInformation.description: Everything smartctl reports about the disk (its --xall output), as display text with newlines. Shown as preformatted text, never as markup.

SmartScheduleEntry.description: A scheduled S.M.A.R.T. self-test with its disk as the system sees it now. When the disk is not present, `devicefile`, `model` and `serialnumber` are empty, `devicelinks` is empty and `size` is "-1".

devicefile.description: The disk's device file under /dev, such as "/dev/sda" (not the stored by-id link that Smart.getScheduledTest returns); empty when the disk is not present.

type.description: S short, L long, C conveyance, O offline. Open to other values.

size.description: Bytes; "-1" when the disk is not present.

SmartScheduleList.description: Every scheduled S.M.A.R.T. self-test, paged and sorted by the backend.

SmartScheduledTest.description: A stored scheduled S.M.A.R.T. self-test (conf.service.smartmontools.job). It runs on the schedule once the pending changes are applied. The schedule fields are "*" or a zero-padded number.

devicefile.description: The disk's /dev/disk/by-id/ link where it has one.

type.description: S short, L long, C conveyance, O offline. Open to other values.

SmartSetScheduledTestRequest.description: A scheduled S.M.A.R.T. self-test (rpc.smart.setscheduledtest). Every field is required. The schedule fields use patterns that are anchored, accepting exactly the values the stock form offers: "*" for every one, or a zero-padded number.

type.description: S a short self-test, L a long (extended) one, C a conveyance test (after transport; not every disk supports it), O an immediate offline test.

MdArray.description: A software RAID array (Linux MD) that the kernel has assembled, as mdadm reports it. Read from the RAID plugin (openmediavault-md).

_used.description: Whether the array holds a file system OMV has set up, or is itself a member of other storage (such as an LVM group).

name.description: mdadm's array name, "host:name", as its brief report gives it. Empty for an array made on this NAS (mdadm 4.4 leaves the name out of that report for its own host's arrays, observed on the test VM); an array made on another computer has that computer's name before the colon.

devicefile.description: The array's device file, such as "/dev/md0".

uuid.description: mdadm's UUID of the array, four groups of eight hex digits joined by colons.

level.description: The RAID level as mdadm names it, such as "raid1", "raid5" or "raid10".

numdevices.description: How many member devices the array is made for. A degraded array has fewer in `devices`.

devices.description: The member devices the array has now, as device files under /dev (a whole disk such as "/dev/sdb", or a partition such as "/dev/sdb1"), in natural order. A failed member is still listed until it is taken out, and spares are listed too (observed on the test VM), so this says nothing about what each one is doing: MdMgmt.getDetail does. A missing member is not listed.

state.description: Display text from mdadm, such as "clean", "active", "clean, degraded" or "clean, degraded, recovering (12.5% (…) finish=…)", with the kernel's progress of a resync, rebuild or reshape appended in brackets. Open: read it as text, not as a list of values. The boolean false when the kernel's RAID status does not list the array (read from the plugin's source).

syncaction.description: What the array is doing now: "idle", "resync", "recover", "check", "repair", "reshape" or "frozen". null for a level without redundancy, such as raid0.

description.description: Display text, "Software RAID", the name and the device, level and size in brackets, such as "Software RAID  [/dev/md0, raid1, 7.99 GiB]" (an empty name leaves two spaces).

MdArrayList.description: Every software RAID array the kernel has assembled, in no particular order; empty when there is none.

MdArrayDeviceFile.description: A software RAID array by its kernel device file, "/dev/md" and its number, such as "/dev/md0". Stricter than OMV's `devicefile` format, which takes any path under /dev: the interface names an array only by the `devicefile` that MdMgmt.enumerateDevices reported for it, and OMV numbers new arrays from 0.

MdDeviceFileRequest.description: One software RAID array, by its device file (rpc.common.devicefile).

MdDetailText.description: mdadm's report on the array (`mdadm --detail` without its first line), as display text in English: one "Key : value" line per fact (Raid Level, Array Size, State, Name, UUID and others), then a table with one line per member: its number, major and minor numbers, its slot in the array (RaidDevice, "-" for a spare or failed member), its state in mdadm's words ("active sync", "spare", "spare rebuilding", "faulty", "removed") and its device file (none for "removed"). Lines such as "Resync Status : 45% complete" or "Reshape Status" appear only while that work runs. Read it as text: the layout is mdadm's, not OMV's.

MdDisk.description: A disk as the RAID plugin lists it: a candidate for a new array (MdMgmt.getCandidates) or a member of one (MdMgmt.getSlaves).

devicefile.description: The disk's device file, such as "/dev/sdb" (a candidate) or the member's name as mdadm lists it (a member). Not the stable /dev/disk/by-id/ name: match it to DiskMgmt.getList by `canonicaldevicefile`.

vendor.description: The vendor the disk reports, such as "ATA"; may be empty.

serialnumber.description: The serial number the disk reports; may be empty.

description.description: Server display text in English, such as "VMware Virtual SATA Hard Drive [/dev/sdb, 8.00 GiB]".

MdDiskList.description: Disks as the RAID plugin lists them, in no particular order; empty when there is none.

MdMgmtCreateRequest.description: The disks of a new array and its level (rpc.mdmgmt.create). The server erases and uses every disk it is given; it checks neither that a disk is a candidate nor that it is empty. Stricter than OMV: at least two disks, each once, and no array name.

devices.description: The disks to erase and make into the array, by their stable /dev/disk/by-id/ names (the `devicefile` of DiskMgmt.getList), each once. mdadm accepts these names and the array then lists its members by their kernel names (observed on the test VM). The level sets the least number the array can be made of: 2 for mirror and stripe, 3 for raid5, 4 for raid6 and raid10 (the plugin's own form); the interface checks this before calling.

name.description: The array's own name. Accepted only empty: the interface gives arrays no name, as the stock form never does, and mdadm then names the array after the host and its number.

level.description: The RAID level, in the plugin's words: "mirror" (RAID1), "raid5", "raid6", "raid10", or "stripe" (RAID0). A stripe has no protection at all: if one of its disks fails, everything on all of them is lost.

MdChange.description: The record of a change the RAID plugin sends to OMV's configuration (conf.system.mdadm.device), returned as the method's reply. It is not stored: OMV writes its arrays down again from mdadm when the mdadm module is applied. Read `devicefile` from it; the other fields describe the request more than the array.

name.description: For create, the name sent (empty); for the other methods, mdadm's "host:name" of the array.

devicefile.description: The array's device file, such as "/dev/md0".

level.description: For create, the level sent ("mirror", "raid5", …); for the other methods, mdadm's ("raid1", "raid5", …).

numdevices.description: The number of disks the server computed: for create, the disks sent; for add and grow, the array's count before plus the disks sent; for delete, the array's count. For remove it is the count before plus the disks taken out (the plugin adds where it should subtract), so it is not the array's new count; read MdMgmt.enumerateDevices for that.

devices.description: For create, the disks as sent; for add, grow and remove, the members mdadm listed before the call with the disks sent added or taken away; for delete, the members mdadm listed.

MdMgmtAddRequest.description: The array and the disk to add to it (rpc.mdmgmt.add). Stricter than OMV, which takes several disks at once: one disk at a time.

devices.description: The disk to erase and add, by its stable /dev/disk/by-id/ name; exactly one. The server checks nothing about it, not even that it is as large as the array's disks.

MdMgmtGrowRequest.description: The array to make bigger and the disks to add to it (rpc.mdmgmt.grow). Stricter than OMV: each disk once.

devices.description: The disks to erase and add, by their stable /dev/disk/by-id/ names, one or more, each once.

MdMgmtRemoveRequest.description: The array and the member to take out of it (rpc.mdmgmt.remove). Stricter than OMV, which takes several members at once: one at a time.

devices.description: The member to take out, as the array lists it in MdMgmt.enumerateDevices `devices` (a kernel name such as "/dev/sdb"); exactly one. The server checks nothing about what is left.

MdMgmtSetSyncActionRequest.description: The array and what its disks should do now (rpc.mdmgmt.setsyncaction). Stricter than OMV, which also takes "repair": the interface offers no repair, because it rewrites one copy from another where they differ, and which copy is right cannot be known from the page.

action.description: "check": read every disk of the array and compare the copies, which takes hours and changes nothing. "idle": stop a check that is running.

FileSystemMgmtCreateRequest.description: The device to erase and the file system to create on it (rpc.filesystemmgmt.create). OMV accepts any type it has a backend for; the contract accepts only the four the interface offers (JFS and the rest are left to the classic interface).

FileSystemMgmtCreateBtrfsRequest.description: The disks to erase and combine into one BTRFS file system, and how (rpc.filesystemmgmt.createbtrfs). Stricter than OMV: two or more devices (one disk uses FileSystemMgmt.create), no `dup` profile, and no `label`, which the interface does not set.

profile.description: How data and metadata are kept: raid1 a mirror (each block on two disks), raid10 mirrored stripes (four disks or more), raid0 striped with no copy, single joined with no copy. With single the server keeps metadata twice (dup); otherwise metadata uses the same profile. The server does not check the number of disks a profile needs.

devicefiles.description: The devices, as OMV takes them: one string of device files separated by commas with no spaces ("/dev/sdb,/dev/sdc"), not a list. Each part is in OMV's `devicefile` format. The server does not refuse a device named twice.

FileSystemMgmtSetMountPointRequest.description: The file system to set up for mounting, with its warning level and tags (rpc.filesystemmgmt.setMountPoint). OMV also accepts the file system's UUID as `id`; the contract accepts only a device file, as getMountCandidates reports it.

usagewarnthreshold.description: Percent used at which OMV warns; 0 means it never warns. The server stores 0 when it is left out.

comment.description: The tags, as one string with "," between them. The server stores "" when it is left out.

MountEntry.description: OMV's mount entry for a file system (conf.system.filesystem.mountpoint): where and how it is mounted, its warning level and its tags. Other configuration, such as a shared folder's `mntentref`, refers to it by `uuid`.

fsname.description: The file system, as OMV records it: a predictable device file (a /dev/disk/by-uuid/ link first) for one mounted through this interface or the classic one, or a UUID or folder for older and add-on entries.

dir.description: The folder it is mounted on.

type.description: The file system type, such as "ext4".

opts.description: The mount options, separated by commas, as OMV chose them for the type and the disk.

hidden.description: Whether OMV keeps it out of /etc/fstab (a type mounted another way).

usagewarnthreshold.description: Percent used at which OMV warns; 0 means it never warns.

comment.description: The tags, as one string. The classic interface writes several tags joined by "," with no space, sorted and without repeats ("Media,Photos").

FsUuid.description: A file system's own UUID, in OMV's `fsuuid` format: a standard UUID (EXT4, XFS, BTRFS), the short FAT and exFAT form "ABCD-1234", the 16-digit NTFS form, or the time stamp a CD or DVD carries ("2026-11-19-05-53-43-00"). It is made when the file system is created and says nothing about the disk.

FileSystemMgmtGrowRequest.description: The file system to grow, by its own UUID (rpc.filesystemmgmt.grow).

MountDir.description: The folder a file system is mounted on, as FileSystemMgmt.getList reports it in `mountpoint` (OMV makes it "/srv/dev-disk-by-uuid-…"). OMV's `dirpath` format, and stricter: an absolute path, never "/" itself, with no ".." step at all, and ASCII only.

FileSystemMgmtUmountByDirRequest.description: The folder of the file system to unmount and forget (rpc.filesystemmgmt.umountbydir). Stricter than OMV's `dirpath`: an absolute folder, never the system's root.

FilesystemDetails.description: The file system's own report, as display text with newlines: dumpe2fs for EXT4 (its superblock, then one section per block group, so hundreds of lines on a large disk), xfs_info for XFS, and for BTRFS the output of "btrfs filesystem show", "filesystem df", "device stats" and "scrub status". The EXT4 report contains the file system's UUID. Shown as preformatted text, never as markup.

FsTabGetByFsNameRequest.description: The file system whose mount entry to find (rpc.fstab.getbyfsname): its UUID or one of its device files. The server also looks under the file system's other device files and its UUID, so any of them finds the entry.

FsTabEntryOrNone.description: The mount entry, or the boolean false when OMV has none for the file system (FsTab.getByFsName returns false rather than failing).

DirPath.description: A folder path, in OMV's `dirpath` format: letters, digits, "_", "-", ".", "/", "@" and spaces, with no "../" step. OMV's check also accepts letters outside ASCII; the contract does not.

FsTabSetRequest.description: A mount entry to store (rpc.fstab.set), as FsTab.getByFsName returned it with the warning level or tags changed. The interface sends every other field back unchanged: the server does not check `fsname`, `dir`, `type` or `opts` against the file system, and a change to them is not applied to the system until the mount module is applied for another reason. With OMV's placeholder UUID it would create a second entry; the interface creates entries only through FileSystemMgmt.setMountPoint. `hidden` is not in OMV's request model, but the stored object has it and the classic form sends it back.

usagewarnthreshold.description: Percent used at which OMV warns; 0 means it never warns.

comment.description: The tags, as one string with "," between them.

ZfsCompressionTypeList.description: The compression names the plugin's classic forms offer ("gzip", "gzip-1" … "zstd-fast-1000"), a fixed list in its source. "off", "on" and "lz4" are not all among them; the interface does not use the list.

ZfsObject.description: One row of the plugin's flat list of pools, file systems and volumes. Each pool comes twice: as its pool row (type "Pool", with the pool's state and its disks' raw space, parity included for RAID-Z) and as the pool's own folder (type "Filesystem", poolroot true, with the space for files). A field that does not apply to a row's type holds "n/a" (observed on the test VM). Sizes are bytes as JSON numbers.

id.description: The plugin's tree id ("root/pool-tank/media"); not a ZFS name.

name.description: A pool's name, the pool's own folder's name (the pool's), or the last part of a file system's or volume's full name ("media").

icon.description: An image of the classic interface; not used.

path.description: The full ZFS name ("tank", "tank/media"); the one name every other method takes.

pool.description: The pool a file system or volume is on. Absent on a pool row.

origin.description: The snapshot a clone was made from ("tank/media@…"), or "n/a" for anything that is not a clone.

size.description: A pool row: the disks' raw space, parity included for RAID-Z (not space for files). A file system: its size limit (quota), or null with none. A volume: its size.

used.description: Bytes in use: a pool row, the disks' raw space allocated (parity included); a file system, what it and everything inside it hold.

usedpercent.description: The plugin's percentage of used, with a fraction. Not used by the interface.

available.description: Bytes free: a pool row, the disks' raw space free; a file system, the pool's free space it may use, or what is left under its size limit.

mountpoint.description: The folder it is mounted on ("/tank/media"); empty when it has none, "n/a" for a volume.

lastscrub.description: A pool row: the plugin's words for the last check: "Never", "in progress since <date>", "paused (started <date>)", "canceled on <date>", or the date it ended, which may be the end of a rebuild rather than of a check. "n/a" on other rows. Display text in English.

state.description: A pool row: ZFS's word for the pool ("ONLINE", "DEGRADED", "FAULTED", "SUSPENDED", "UNAVAIL", "REMOVED", "OFFLINE"), or "UNKNOWN" when the plugin could not read it. "n/a" on other rows.

status.description: A pool row: "OK", or "Error" when ZFS counts damaged data. "n/a" on other rows.

scrubstate.description: A pool row: "none", "running", "paused", "stopped" or "completed" (the last check or rebuild). "n/a" on other rows.

scrubactive.description: Whether a check is running or paused on the pool.

removalactive.description: A pool row only: whether data is being moved off a disk group that is being removed.

hasshares.description: Whether a shared folder uses its mount entry.

dedup.description: A pool row only. The deduplication ratio, "1.00" for none (no "x").

capacity.description: A pool row only: whole percent of the disks' raw space in use. ZFS slows down and refuses writes by this figure.

devices.description: A pool row only: the disks' paths joined with a markup line break. Not used (UI-2); the disks come from Zfs.getPoolDevices.

compression.description: Not on a pool row: the compression in effect ("lz4", "off", "zstd", …), inherited or its own.

compressratio.description: Not on a pool row. The compression ratio, "1.00" for none (no "x").

refer.description: Not on a pool row. Bytes it refers to itself, without what is inside it.

poolroot.description: A file system row only. True for the pool's own folder.

haschildren.description: Whether file systems, volumes or snapshots are inside it.

ZfsObjectList.description: Every pool, file system and volume, in the plugin's order (each pool, then its own folder, then what is inside it), paged by the backend.

ZfsPoolName.description: An existing pool's name, as Zfs.listPools gives it in `name` (design phase-5-zfs 0.7): a letter first, then up to 63 letters, digits, "_", ".", ":" or "-". Stricter than the plugin, which checks nothing. A pool whose name is outside this has no page in the interface and is managed in the classic one.

ZfsDatasetName.description: An existing pool or file system by its full name, as Zfs.listPools gives it in `path` ("tank", "tank/media"; design phase-5-zfs 0.7): the pool's name, then up to 8 parts after "/", each a letter or digit first and then up to 63 letters, digits, "_", ".", ":" or "-" (so never "." or ".."), 255 characters in all. Stricter than the plugin, which checks nothing.

ZfsFilesystemDetailsRequest.description: A file system's report, the pool's own folder included.

ZfsGetObjectDetailsRequest.description: Which report (rpc.zfs.objectdetails): a pool's, by its name, or a file system's, by its full name. Stricter than the plugin, which also reports on volumes and snapshots and checks no name.

ZfsReport.description: ZFS's own report, as display text, lines joined by a line feed and a carriage return: for a pool, "Pool status (zpool status -v):" then zpool status's report (its state, the scan line of the last or running check or rebuild, the device tree with each device's state and error counts, and the errors line, with damaged files' paths when there are any); for a file system, "Filesystem status (zfs list):", one zfs list line, and every property from zfs get all, which includes the file system's GUID. Shown as preformatted text, never as markup.

ZfsPoolNameRequest.description: One pool by its name (rpc.zfs.name). Stricter than the plugin: the name is an existing pool's, in the form ZfsPoolName allows.

ZfsPoolDevice.description: A disk of a pool, from zpool status's structured report: data disks, spares, read caches, write logs and metadata disks alike.

devicefile.description: The path ZFS opened it by, such as "/dev/disk/by-id/ata-…-part1" for a whole disk ZFS partitioned. A disk that is missing keeps the path it was last seen at.

state.description: ZFS's word for the disk in capitals: "ONLINE", "DEGRADED", "FAULTED", "UNAVAIL", "REMOVED", "OFFLINE", or for a spare "AVAIL" or "INUSE".

vdev.description: The group it is in ("mirror-0", "raidz1-0", "replacing-1" while it is being replaced), or empty for a disk directly under the pool (a single disk or a stripe).

label.description: Display text in English for the classic interface; not shown.

ZfsPoolDeviceList.description: The disks of one pool. Empty when the pool does not exist or ZFS could not be asked (the plugin answers both with an empty list, not an error).

ZfsPoolStatus.description: One pool's state and how full it is.

state.description: ZFS's word for the pool: "ONLINE", "DEGRADED", "FAULTED", "SUSPENDED", "UNAVAIL", "REMOVED" or "OFFLINE".

status.description: "OK", or "Error" when ZFS counts damaged data.

capacity.description: Whole percent of the disks' raw space in use.

ZfsPoolStatusList.description: Every pool, by name. Empty when there is none, and also when ZFS could not be asked (the plugin answers both the same way).

ZfsSnapshot.description: A snapshot. The reply does not say when it was taken; a snapshot taken here is named by it.

id.description: The plugin's tree id; not a ZFS name.

parent.description: The full name of the file system or volume it is a snapshot of.

name.description: Its own name, the part after "@". Zfs.quickSnapshot names it by the NAS's date and time, "YYYY-MM-DD_hh-mm-ss".

path.description: Its full name ("tank/media@…"), the one name every other method takes.

used.description: Bytes only this snapshot holds, which deleting it frees.

refer.description: Bytes of the file system as the snapshot keeps it.

ZfsSnapshotList.description: Every snapshot on every pool, in name order, paged by the backend.

ZfsCandidate.description: A disk the plugin offers for a new pool or as a replacement.

devicefile.description: The disk's stable /dev/disk/by-id/ name, the one to send to Zfs.addPool and Zfs.deviceReplace; its kernel name only when it has no by-id link.

vendor.description: The vendor the disk reports, such as "ATA"; may be empty.

serialnumber.description: The serial number the disk reports; may be empty.

description.description: Server display text in English, such as "VMware Virtual SATA Hard Drive [/dev/sdb, 8.00 GiB]".

label.description: The description with the serial number, display text in English; not shown.

ZfsCandidateList.description: The disks the plugin offers: not read-only, not connected by USB, not named by another service's settings, not in use, and with no file system or partition table found on them. A disk of a deleted pool keeps ZFS's partition table and is not offered until it is wiped (observed on the test VM).

ZfsNewPoolName.description: The name of a new pool (design phase-5-zfs 0.7): 1 to 32 letters, digits, "-" or "_", a letter first; not a word ZFS keeps for itself (a name starting with mirror, raidz, draid or spare, or "log"), and not the name of a folder the system uses at the top of the disk (bin, boot, dev, etc, home, lib, lib32, lib64, media, mnt, opt, proc, root, run, sbin, srv, sys, tmp, usr, var), case ignored, because the pool's folder is /<name>. Stricter than the plugin, which refuses only a space, and than ZFS. Whether a pool of the name exists already is the interface's own check.

ZfsDiskById.description: A disk, or a partition ZFS made on one, by its stable /dev/disk/by-id/ name: as Zfs.getEmptyCandidates gives it for a new disk, and as Zfs.getPoolDevices gives it for a disk in a pool ("…-part1" for a whole disk ZFS partitioned). A letter or digit first, then letters, digits, ".", "_", ":", "+" or "-", and no "/". Stricter than OMV's device-file format and than the plugin, which checks nothing for a disk already in a pool: a disk renamed between a read and the call is never hit by mistake, and a pool whose disks ZFS names otherwise (by kernel name or by path) is not changed through this contract.

ZfsAddPoolRequest.description: A new pool of one group of disks (rpc.zfs.addpool), with the interface's fixed settings (design phase-5-zfs 12.1, D11 to D13). Stricter than the plugin: every setting but the layout, the name and the disks has the one value the interface sends; the disks are by their stable by-id names; and compress and compresstype, which the plugin reads though its datamodel does not declare them, are required as "on, LZ4".

pooltype.description: How the disks are arranged, in the plugin's words: "mirror" (every disk a copy), "raidz1", "raidz2" and "raidz3" (one, two or three disks' worth of parity), or "basic" (one disk, or several striped: no protection at all; if one disk fails, everything on the pool is lost). The least number of disks is 2 for mirror, 3, 4 and 5 for raidz1 to raidz3, and 1 for basic; ZFS refuses fewer, and the interface checks it before calling.

force.description: Whether ZFS may overwrite a disk that looks in use. Accepted only false: the interface never forces (D12), so ZFS refuses a disk that holds a pool or a file system.

mountpoint.description: The pool's folder. Accepted only empty: ZFS's default, /<name> (D13).

devices.description: The disks to erase and make into the pool, by the by-id names Zfs.getEmptyCandidates gives, each once.

devalias.description: How ZFS is to name the disks. Accepted only "id": by their stable by-id names (D12).

ashift.description: Whether ashiftval is set. Accepted only true (D12).

ashiftval.description: The block size as a power of two. Accepted only 12, 4 KiB blocks (D12).

casesensitivity.description: Whether file names differ by case. Accepted only "sensitive" (D12).

compress.description: Whether compression is turned on after the pool is made. Read by the plugin though its datamodel does not declare it. Accepted only true (D11).

compresstype.description: The compression, when compress is true. Read by the plugin though its datamodel does not declare it. Accepted only "lz4" (D11).

ZfsNewFilesystemName.description: The name of a new file system at the top of a pool, without the pool's name (design phase-5-zfs 0.7): 1 to 64 letters, digits, "-", "_" or ".", a letter or digit first (so never "." or ".."), and no "/", because the plugin creates every missing parent ("zfs create -p"). Stricter than the plugin, which refuses only a space. The plugin does not refuse a name that is taken: it answers as if it had created it (observed on the test VM), so that is the interface's own check.

ZfsAddObjectRequest.description: A new file system at the top of a pool (rpc.zfs.addobject). Stricter than the plugin, which also makes snapshots, volumes and clones with this method: only a file system, on an existing pool, in its default folder, with no property of its own (it inherits the pool's compression).

mountpoint.description: The file system's folder. Accepted only empty: ZFS's default, /<pool>/<name> (D13).

ZfsQuotaProperty.description: A file system's size limit: "none" for no limit, or a whole number of GiB or TiB ("500G", "2T"). ZFS refuses a limit below what the file system holds (HTTP 500, observed on the test VM); the interface checks it first.

ZfsCompressionProperty.description: A file system's compression, on ("lz4") or off.

ZfsSetPropertiesRequest.description: New values for a file system's properties (rpc.zfs.setproperties). Stricter than the plugin, which sets any property of a pool, file system, volume or snapshot: only a file system's size limit and compression, one of each at most, each marked modified, which the plugin requires though its datamodel does not declare it (an item not marked is skipped).

ZfsQuickSnapshotRequest.description: A file system to take a snapshot of now (rpc.zfs.quicksnapshot). Stricter than the plugin: the name is an existing pool's or file system's, and recursive is always sent.

recursive.description: Whether the file systems inside it are snapshotted too, at the same moment.

ZfsSnapshotPath.description: A snapshot by its full name, as Zfs.getAllSnapshots gives it in `path` ("tank/media@<name>"): a ZfsDatasetName, "@", and the snapshot's own name, a letter or digit first and then up to 63 letters, digits, "_", ".", ":" or "-". Stricter than the plugin, which checks nothing.

ZfsSnapshotRequest.description: One snapshot by its full name (rpc.zfs.name). Stricter than the plugin: only a snapshot's full name, in the form ZfsSnapshotPath allows.

ZfsDeleteSnapshotRequest.description: A snapshot to delete. It has no folder of its own, so mp is empty.

ZfsFilesystemName.description: An existing file system on a pool, not the pool's own folder, by its full name ("tank/media"): as ZfsDatasetName, with at least one part after the pool's name.

ZfsMountFolder.description: The folder a pool or file system is mounted on, as Zfs.listPools gives it in `mountpoint` ("/tank/media"): an absolute path of letters, digits, "_", ".", ":", "+" and "-", with no "." or ".." part, and never "/" itself. The interface sends the folder Zfs.listPools gave for the object it deletes, after its own check of what uses it (design phase-5-zfs 0.10).

ZfsDeleteFilesystemRequest.description: A file system to delete, with everything in it and all its snapshots, by its full name and the folder it is mounted on.

ZfsDeletePoolRequest.description: A pool to delete, by its name and the folder its own folder is mounted on. The plugin refuses while it holds any file system or volume.

ZfsDeleteObjectRequest.description: What to delete (rpc.zfs.deleteobject): a snapshot, a file system other than a pool's own folder, or a pool. Stricter than the plugin, which also deletes volumes and deletes recursively: never a volume, never recursive, and each name in the form of its kind.

ZfsDeviceReplaceRequest.description: A disk of a pool and the disk to put in its place (rpc.zfs.pooltwodevices). Stricter than the plugin, which checks nothing: the old disk by the by-id name Zfs.getPoolDevices gives for it, the new one by the by-id name Zfs.getEmptyCandidates gives.

ZfsPoolDeviceRequest.description: One disk of a pool (rpc.zfs.pooldevice). Stricter than the plugin, which checks nothing: the pool by its name and the disk by the by-id name Zfs.getPoolDevices gives for it.

SmartDevice.description: A disk that supports S.M.A.R.T., with its health as smartctl last reported it.

devicename.description: The kernel's name for the disk, such as "sda".

canonicaldevicefile.description: The device file under /dev, such as "/dev/sda".

temperature.description: Degrees Celsius: a whole number, or the same number as text (observed for an NVMe disk on OMV 8.6.1). The empty string when the disk reports none or could not be read.

description.description: Display text, such as "VMware Virtual NVMe Disk [/dev/nvme0n1, 20.00 GiB]".

wwn.description: The disk's World Wide Name; the empty string when it has none.

overallstatus.description: The disk's health: GOOD; BAD_ATTRIBUTE_IN_THE_PAST (was used outside its design limits); BAD_SECTOR (a few bad sectors); BAD_ATTRIBUTE_NOW (used outside its design limits now); BAD_SECTOR_MANY (many bad sectors); BAD_STATUS (unknown: smartctl could not read the disk's health, as for disks that do not report it, such as some virtual disks). Open to other values, so a later OMV's value is shown as unknown rather than refused.

uuid.description: The disk's monitoring settings object, or OMV's placeholder for an object not yet saved (fa4b1c66-ef79-11e5-87a0-0002b3a176b4) when monitoring was never set up for it.

monitor.description: Whether S.M.A.R.T. monitoring is turned on for this disk.

_used.description: Whether a scheduled S.M.A.R.T. test refers to this disk.

FilesystemCandidate.description: A device the server offers for a new file system: not read-only, holding no file system, and with no partition table, file system, RAID or other signature left on it.

description.description: Server display text in English, such as "VMware Virtual SATA Hard Drive [/dev/sdb, 8.00 GiB]".
